title: Entropy Deficit of Activity Screening at the Critical Expected Response Budget
banked_reason: D0.5 REVISE: sound sharp subcritical and infinitesimal-surplus theorem, but kernel_substituted@oeq:joint-frontier leaves the promised every-sequence positive-surplus frontier open.
gap_reasons: The promised every-sequence critical-budget frontier has been replaced by a proved subcritical/|B_s-3/2|=o(h_s) result: the required evaluable Psi, matching all-policy comparison, and legal attainers across nontrivial supercritical windows remain an open question.

The delivered sharp theorem establishes D_B(s)=L(3/2−B)+(3^{1/6}/2)h_s+o(h_s) uniformly below the boundary, and the critical coefficient for signed displacements o(h_s). It does not determine the positive-surplus crossover when (B_s−3/2)/h_s approaches a positive constant, or the farther-supercritical windows required by the every-sequence joint-frontier target. The O(eta_s) selective-recovery comparison supplies no matching relative characterization when the deficit is comparable to or smaller than eta_s, leaving the leading contribution of selected continuation and additional responses unresolved. The TL;DR and justification accurately restrict their established claims, so there is no stale assertion that the full joint frontier is proved. The threshold hierarchy is credited to the unpublished internal parent, while generic selective ordering is antecedent material in the [public comparator theorem and proof](https://bradleyrava.github.io/Papers/theory_indecisions.pdf). The score reflects a specialized partial boundary result for one two-factor prior, with the positive-surplus budgeting law and relative original-experiment certificate still absent; those substantive limits survive competent rewriting. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: One D0 solve round established a sharp subcritical expansion with coefficient 3^(1/6)/2 and an infinitesimal signed-surplus extension; the math panel passed those scoped claims. The decision panel retained kernel_substituted@oeq:joint-frontier because positive-surplus windows, vanishing multipliers, selected continuation/later responses, and a relative original-experiment certificate remain open; the delivered score ceiling 5.6 is below the field floor 7.4. Independent main terminal validity confirms downgraded stop; graph fsck verified all 16 commits, while no Lean formalization or type-checker verification was attempted.
tldr: For the two-activity Gaussian-slab experiment with persistent hidden inverse-gamma noise, the critical expected response budget is 3/2. Uniformly for 1≤B≤3/2, the original-policy entropy deficit is L(3/2−B)+(3^(1/6)/2)h_s+o(h_s), with h_s=s^(−1/6)sqrt(log s); the converse retains the expected cost of responses beyond the second, and total observable two-response posterior-quantile policies attain the expansion at the declared budget. The same critical term holds for every signed sequence B_s−3/2=o(h_s). The nontrivial positive-surplus joint profile, selected-continuation recovery below additive eta_s accuracy, and arbitrary-relative certificate remain open. The identical-model budget-two parent and its cost-3/2 hierarchy retain full priority.
gap: The scoped primary stopping and screening theorems provide posterior selection, information accounting and expected-cost comparisons. The identical-model parent targets the full \(B=2\) frontier. These objects do not determine the first nonzero deficit uniformly as \(B_s\to B_{\mathrm{crit}}\).
fill: An explicitly reduced joint entropy-cost experiment, matched to the entire observable policy class and recovered at relative precision, determines the windows and implementing budget choices.
